pi.name: Professor Vassilios Morellas
pi.title: Research Professor
pi.bio: Professor Vassilios Morellas's research interests are in the area of geometric image processing, machine learning, robotics, and sensor integration to enhance the automation of electromechanical systems. He is program director in the Department of Computer Science & Engineering and executive director of the NSF Center for Safety Security and Rescue. Prior to his current position, he was a senior principle research scientist at Honeywell Laboratories, where he developed technologies in the general areas of access control, security, and surveillance and biometrics with emphasis on the problem of tracking of people and vehicles across non-overlapping cameras. His past research experience also includes work on intelligent transformation systems, where he developed innovative technologies to reduce run-off-the-road accidents. Morellas obtained his diploma degree in mechanical engineering from the National Technical University of Athens, Greece, his MSME degree from Columbia University, and his PhD degree from the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Minnesota. He publishes regularly in peer-reviewed conference proceedings and journals and has coauthored a book on camera programming.

pi.name: Ted Morris
pi.title: Research Engineer
pi.bio: Ted Morris has worked across various application domains within Intelligent Transportation Systems, including self-driving/driver-assist heavy vehicles, mobile, and roadside computer vision sensing for evaluating and monitoring road user and traffic behaviors. As a MnRI research engineer, he co-leads and serves as the primary technical liaison for research projects for real-time, regionwide, truck parking monitoring and general- vulnerable road user behavior monitoring for applications to connected and autonomous vehicles. His research interests include VR immersive environments and sensing for human neurophysiologic and cognitive behavior assessment and collaborative robotic applications.
